items.title: THIS IS F*CKING UNREAL, META MUSE EMBER TURNED A CLAUDE HAIKU 5.5 SCORE INTO A FRACTION OF THE COST
items.summary:
THIS IS F*CKING UNREAL, META MUSE EMBER TURNED A CLAUDE HAIKU 5.5 SCORE INTO A FRACTION OF THE COST
SAME $0.10 / $0.50 PRICE AS GPT-6 LUNA. $0.14 A TASK VS $0.41

artificial analysis index: ember 36, claude haiku 5.5 36, gpt-6 luna 28. the trick is not the price list:          

to run the index, haiku 5.5 at max wrote 298M output tokens. ember wrote 115M. same $0.50 rate, 2.6x fewer tokens, that's the whole gap

the job: the steps an agent repeats all day. tool calls, routing, extraction, small code fixes. what you see: the same answers on a smaller bill

meta's own pitch is a planner + worker split: muse wonder plans, ember handles the volume. on a claude desk the same split is claude opus plans, claude haiku executes. a day on that desk looks like this:

→ 09:00 opus reads the queue once and writes the plan
→ 09:05 the cheap worker runs the tool calls and extractions, hundreds of them
→ 13:00 the worker fixes small failing tests, opus reviews anything that becomes a PR
→ 18:00 cost report: tokens per task per model, not per million

the numbers, all three at max reasoning:

automationbench (artificial analysis, 657 zapier workflows): ember 37.8%, haiku 5.5 13.9%, luna 20.2%
coding agent index (each model in its own agent): ember 46, haiku 37, luna 31
frontiercode 2.0, merge-ready code: haiku 5.5 wins 34.9 vs 27.2

two catches. 4 of meta's 10 rows are meta's own runs. and past 200K tokens ember's price triples to $0.30 / $1.50 (haiku 5.5 already steps up past 100K, to $0.50 / $2.50)

so the worker slot is open for a test, the merge slot stays with claude. give claude code last week of your agent logs, then ask:

"1. tag every model call as plan, tool call, extraction, small fix or PR. do not edit any config.

2. for each tag, compute cost per task at the listed prices of claude haiku 5.5, gpt-6 luna and muse ember, using the real token counts, not per-million prices. show the math.

3. pick one tag where a cheaper worker could fit and draft a 5% shadow test: same inputs, outputs logged side by side, nothing sent to users or merged without my yes.

4. flag every prompt over 100K and 200K tokens, because both price lists step up there."

start with one tag before expanding

worker slot: ember or haiku?

知財関係者（特に、特許担当者) のコメントを求む ! !

⑪ 「法令上の公報」（XML形式）は、実際に使われているのでしょうか？

特許庁の審判では使われていません。

2022年１月１２日以降の公報。

特許庁は、「法令上の公報は、公報発行サイトから提供されるものであって、XML形式のものを指します。」と明言しています。

そして、「ＸＭＬ形式」とは、以下の資料のフロントページにあるようなものです。

https://t.co/bHC0RUmH1C   

また、2022年１月１１日以前に特許庁より発行されていた「PDF公報」は、廃止されました。

従来は、この廃止されたPDF公報が「真正な公報」とみなされてきたと思います。

何となれば、特許庁が発行するものが唯一のものでしたので。

2022年１月１２日以降は、INPITをはじめ、多くの民間のベンダーが独自の手法により作成したものが、「独自PDF公報」として流通しています。

そして、INPITは、「公報はＸＭＬですので、レイアウトもページも存在しません。」、「したがって、公報標準レイアウト/ページの概念はございません。」ともいっています。

更に、「公報はＸＭＬであり、ＰＤＦ化するに当たっての制限はありません。」と断言しています。

加えて、INPITは「J-PlatPatから提供されるPDFを「標準」とする意図はなく、民間事業者が提供するPDFも流通すると考えております。」、と回答しています。

従って、「真正な特許公報」とは、特許庁の公報発行サイトから提供される「XML形式」のみのもので、INPITや各民間業者の作成した「独自PDF公報」は「法令上の公報」とはいえないことになります。

くどいようですが、INPITのJ-PlatPatよりダウンロードして得られる「PDF公報」は、あくまでも「独自PDF公報」であって、「真正な公報」とは言えないものと考えます。
このことを前提に、特許庁内で行われている事象を検証してみたいと思います。
「特許第7,246,755号」（権利者：虻川 卓也）への、「異議申立」（異議2023-700568）（異議申立人：平山巌）についてです。

先ずは、特許庁の公報発行サイトから、特許第7,246,755号の「XML形式」での「法令上の公報」です。

https://t.co/D5Qynn3G9X

次に、INPIT   のJ-PlatPatよりダウンロードした「独自PDF公報」（全頁）と「請求項１〜８」の部分です。

https://t.co/kmSQ550JHG

https://t.co/x2iJyp0L47

そして、本題です。

「特許第7,246,755号」（権利者：虻川 卓也）の「経過記録と異議の決定」にて説明します。

https://t.co/waDw7nmcHE

https://t.co/NgFMNPPLfx

右側の青で囲った「経過記録」の下方に黄色の枠の「異議の決定」（2024/3/24）があります。

この「異議の決定」の文章の一部を切り取って、左側にもってきて、紫色で囲いました。

この中に、「令和５年３月２８日　　　特許掲載公報」とあり、これが上記の「XML形式」の「法令上の公報」が発行され、その発行日と思われます。

第２ 本件発明として、「本件特許の特許請求の範囲は、次のとおりである。そして、請求項１、８に係る発明（以下、それぞれ、「本件発明１」、「本件発明８」という。）は、

特許請求の範囲の請求項１、８に記載された事項により特定されるとおりである。」との記載があります。

そして、その下段に、青色を付した【請求項１】〜【請求項８】が記載されています。

この【請求項１】〜【請求項８】の文面は、何でしょうか？

INPIT のJ-PlatPatよりダウンロードした「独自PDF公報」のうち、「請求項１〜８」の部分と同一です。

多分、この【請求項１】〜【請求項８】は、異議申立人（平山巌）が、異議申立書に添付したものと考えられます。

特許庁は、「法令上の公報は、公報発行サイトから提供されるものであって、XML形式のものを指します。」と明言しています。

何故、「法令上の公報」である「XML形式」のものを対象にしないのでしょうか？

「独自PDF公報」に依存した議論は、全く無意味なものと考えます。

「独自PDF公報」は、従来の特許庁が発行していた「PDF公報」とは、似ても似つかない、単なる「参考資料」としか言えないものと思います。

（中文）

⑪ “法律公报”（XML 格式）是否实际使用？

日本特许厅 (JPO) 的上诉程序中不使用“法律公报”。

2022 年 1 月 12 日之后发布的公报。

日本特许厅明确指出，“法律公报是指公报发布网站提供的 XML 格式公报。”

“XML 格式”类似于以下文档首页的格式：

https://t.co/bHC0RUmH1C

此外，日本特许厅在 2022 年 1 月 11 日之前发布的“PDF 公报”已被废止。

此前，该已废止的 PDF 公报被视为“正式公报”。

这是因为当时只有日本特许厅发布的公报。

自2022年1月12日起，包括INPIT在内的许多私营企业开始分发使用各自方法制作的“专有PDF出版物”。

INPIT还表示，“出版物采用XML格式，因此没有布局或页数限制”，并且“因此不存在标准出版物布局/页数的概念”。

此外，他们还声称“出版物采用XML格式，将其转换为PDF格式没有任何限制”。

另外，INPIT回应称，“无意将J-PlatPat提供的PDF指定为‘标准’，我们认为私营企业提供的PDF也会被分发”。

因此，“真正的专利出版物”仅指日本特许厅出版物网站提供的“XML格式”，而INPIT和各私营企业制作的“专有PDF出版物”不能被视为“法律认可的出版物”。

从INPIT的J-PlatPat下载的“PDF出版物”仅仅是“专有PDF出版物”，不能被视为“真正的出版物”。

鉴于此，让我们来考察一下日本特许局内部发生的事情。

此事涉及对“专利号7,246,755”（权利人：阿武川拓也）的“异议”（异议案号2023-700568）（异议人：平山岩夫）。

首先，从日本特许局的出版物网站上，我们找到了专利号7,246,755的“法律出版物”（XML格式）。

https://t.co/D5Qynn3G9X

接下来，这里是“原始PDF出版物”（所有页面）和“权利要求1-8”，均从INPIT的J-PlatPat下载。

https://t.co/kmSQ550JHG

https://t.co/x2iJyp0L47

现在，进入正题。

我将以“专利号 7,246,755”（权利人：阿武川拓也）的“诉讼记录和异议决定”为例进行说明。

https://t.co/waDw7nmcHE

https://t.co/NgFMNPPLfx

在“进展记录”（右侧蓝色圆圈所示）下方，有一个黄色方框，其中包含“异议决定”（2024年3月24日）。

现在，我们来谈谈重点。

我从这份“异议决定”中提取了一部分文本，将其移至左侧，并用紫色圈出。

这份文件中有一条注释，内容为“专利公报，2023年3月28日”，这很可能是前述“XML格式”法律公报的发布日期。

关于本发明的第2节指出：“本专利的权利要求如下。与权利要求1和8相关的发明（以下分别称为“发明1”和“发明8”）具体内容由权利要求1和8中所述的事项规定。”

其下方，蓝色部分是权利要求1至8。

这些权利要求1至8的内容是什么？

它与从INPIT的J-PlatPat下载的“原始PDF公报”中的“权利要求1至8”部分完全相同。

这些权利要求1至8很可能是异议申请人（平山岩夫）在异议声明中附上的。日本特许厅（JPO）明确指出，“法律公报是指从公报发布网站提供的、采用XML格式的公报。”

为什么不把重点放在“法律公报”的“XML格式”上呢？

我认为，依赖“专有PDF公报”的论点完全没有意义。

“专有PDF公报”只不过是“参考资料”，与日本特许厅之前发布的“PDF公报”没有任何相似之处。

（英文）

Da?n AI .  Don't get addicted to AI ! Don't make AI your lover！ Don't use AI, think and write for yourself !!

Seeking comments from IP professionals (especially patent specialists) ! !

⑪Statutory Gazette under the law

⑪ Are "statutory gazettes" (XML format) actually used?

They are not used in JPO trials.

Gazettes after January 12, 2022.

The JPO clearly states that "statutory gazettes are provided by the gazette issuing website and are in XML format."

The "XML format" refers to the format shown on the front page of the following document:

https://t.co/bHC0RUmH1C

Furthermore, the "PDF gazettes" issued by the JPO before January 11, 2022, have been discontinued.

Until now, I believe these discontinued PDF gazettes have been considered "genuine gazettes."

This is because the one issued by the JPO was the only one.

As of January 12, 2022, INPIT and many other private vendors have been distributing "original PDF gazettes" created using their own methods.

INPIT has also stated that "Since gazettes are XML, there are no layouts or pages," and that "therefore, there is no concept of a standard gazette layout/page."

Furthermore, they have asserted that "Since gazettes are XML, there are no restrictions on converting them to PDF."

In addition, INPIT has stated that "We have no intention of making the PDF provided by J-PlatPat the 'standard,' and we believe that PDFs provided by private companies will also be in circulation."

Therefore, "genuine patent gazettes" are only those in "XML format" provided by the Japan Patent Office's gazette publishing website, and "original PDF gazettes" created by INPIT and private vendors cannot be considered "public gazettes under the law."

The "PDF Gazette" available for download from INPIT's J-PlatPat is merely a "proprietary PDF Gazette," and cannot be considered a "genuine Gazette."

With this in mind, I would like to examine what is happening within the Japan Patent Office.

This is about the "Opposition" (Objection 2023-700568) (Opposer: Hirayama Iwao) against "Patent No. 7,246,755" (Rights holder: Abukawa Takuya).

First, here is the "Legal Gazette" in "XML format" for Patent No. 7,246,755, from the Japan Patent Office's gazette issuance website.

https://t.co/D5Qynn3G9X

Next, here are the "Original PDF Publication" (all pages) and "Claims 1-8" downloaded from INPIT's J-PlatPat.

https://t.co/kmSQ550JHG

https://t.co/x2iJyp0L47

Now, onto the main topic.

This will be explained in the "Progress Record and Opposition Decision" section of "Patent No. 7,246,755" (Owner: Takuya Abukawa).

https://t.co/waDw7nmcHE

https://t.co/NgFMNPPLfx

Below the "Progress Record" circled in blue on the right, you'll find the "Objection Decision" (March 24, 2024) in a yellow box.

I cut out a portion of the text from this "Objection Decision," moved it to the left, and circled it in purple.

It states, "Patent Publication Gazette: March 28, 2023," which is likely the publication date of the above-mentioned "Legal Gazette" in "XML format."

Section 2: Regarding the Invention at Issue, it states, "The claims of the patent at issue are as follows. The inventions claimed in claims 1 and 8 (hereinafter referred to as "Invention 1" and "Invention 8," respectively) are

defined by the matters set forth in claims 1 and 8 of the patent claims."

Subjacent to this are listed [Claim 1] through [Claim 8] in blue.

What do these [Claim 1] through [Claim 8] refer to?

This is the same as the "Claim 1-8" section in the "Proprietary PDF Gazette" downloaded from INPIT's J-PlatPat.

It is likely that [Claim 1] through [Claim 8] were attached to the Notice of Opposition by the opponent (Iwao Hirayama).

The Japan Patent Office has clearly stated that "Legal Gazettes are those provided by the gazette publishing website and are in XML format."

Why not include "XML format" versions of "legal gazettes"?

I believe that discussions relying on "original PDF Gazettes" are completely meaningless.

I believe that "original PDF Gazettes" are nothing like the "PDF Gazettes" previously issued by the Japan Patent Office and can only be described as "reference materials."
 #DamnAI #ClaudeCode

items.title: If it was that simple, we’d already have a 5 trillion model.
items.summary:
If it was that simple, we’d already have a 5 trillion model.

Unfortunately there are limits to the available data and what can be trained into the model. We hit that wall sometime around GPT 4. The scaling phase of LLMs has ended and the quality density phase has begun.

With that said, I don’t think we’ll ever see LLMs writing better code than humans. Regurgitating patterns of code written by others isn’t a very scalable solution, and it can’t exceed the capabilities or quality baked into the training data.

items.title: Accurate medical advice from AI can still be dangerous | STAT
items.summary: Some will argue that AI should be a neutral aggregator of information. But AI cannot be neutral: Every accurate answer excludes many additional facts and emphasizes some over others. Because of these choices, AI answers already influence behavior, as shown by the chickenpox party examples. [...] Artificial intelligence is delivering health guidance at an unprecedented scale. Every week, more than 300 million people ask ChatGPT health questions. Now, the federal government is moving AI deeper into medical care to communicate directly and autonomously with patients. Chris Klomp, the nominee for deputy secretary of Health and Human Services, has called AI in patient care the agency’s “holy grail” for improving the nation’s health. [...] Medical ethics pairs the duty to do no harm with beneficence, which is an affirmative obligation to do good. Safety evaluations of AI have focused mainly on the first duty by screening for responses that encourage imminent self-harm, discourage necessary care, or spread false information. Behavioral benchmarking would extend the first duty beyond imminent danger to long-term harms. It could also advance the second duty, which has received far less attention: designing AI to help people by

items.title: Why is Nvidia so powerful in the AI world, and what could Jensen Huang’s scandal really cost?
items.summary:
The AI sector is notorious for the amount of circular financing going on – where companies invest in their own suppliers or customers. Nvidia is a key player in this loop.

Investors are already fretting over whether the enormous amounts of money sunk into AI can ever return profits.

While leading AI model builders Anthropic and OpenAI are moving toward public listings or fresh funding rounds, both face harsh reality checks. [...] The now multi-trillion-dollar company got its start making chips called graphic processing units (GPUs), used largely for video games. However, these chips – and their successors – turned out to be ideal for the kind of number-crunching needed for training and using AI models.

Other companies such as Google and AMD have tried to make chips that can compete with Nvidia for speed and efficiency, however neither has been able to displace Nvidia from its dominance of the AI market. [...] Computer chips – specifically the chips used to produce and run artificial intelligence (AI) systems – have become a key front in the United States’ rivalry with China for geopolitical power and influence. The most powerful chips are needed for the most advanced AI, and the US has tried to maintain its edge over China by restricting access to those chips.

While the Chinese government rejects claims of espionage, Alice Huang has reportedly been under investigation by the US for years.

items.title: Why is Nvidia so powerful in the AI world, and what could Jensen Huang’s scandal really cost?
items.summary:
The AI sector is notorious for the amount of circular financing going on – where companies invest in their own suppliers or customers. Nvidia is a key player in this loop.

Investors are already fretting over whether the enormous amounts of money sunk into AI can ever return profits.

While leading AI model builders Anthropic and OpenAI are moving toward public listings or fresh funding rounds, both face harsh reality checks. [...] The now multi-trillion-dollar company got its start making chips called graphic processing units (GPUs), used largely for video games. However, these chips – and their successors – turned out to be ideal for the kind of number-crunching needed for training and using AI models.

Other companies such as Google and AMD have tried to make chips that can compete with Nvidia for speed and efficiency, however neither has been able to displace Nvidia from its dominance of the AI market. [...] Computer chips – specifically the chips used to produce and run artificial intelligence (AI) systems – have become a key front in the United States’ rivalry with China for geopolitical power and influence. The most powerful chips are needed for the most advanced AI, and the US has tried to maintain its edge over China by restricting access to those chips.

While the Chinese government rejects claims of espionage, Alice Huang has reportedly been under investigation by the US for years.

items.title: Recent advances in AI are creating a 'paradigm shift' for robotics - Berkeley News
items.summary:
Traditionally, engineers can directly program the software that tells robots how to perceive objects, plan movements and control their actions, a process called model-based robotics. Or, with model-free robotics, they can train robots to learn behaviors from demonstrations through imitation learning. The first approach requires extensive engineering, while the second needs enormous amounts of data and time. [...] Berkeley-based Ambi Robotics, which specializes in logistics and warehouse order fulfillment, applied the new methods earlier this year to analyze parcel sorting data and test updates to robot behavior. Tests showed an increased capacity of over 15,000 packages sorted annually per robot; the change is now deployed across 30% of the company’s U.S. fleet. [...] Ken Goldberg

“Agentic robotics is a fundamental shift in how robots are controlled,” Goldberg said. “Instead of collecting massive amounts of data and hand-tuning every behavior, teams of agents can quickly generate, test and refine robot programs that allow human engineers to interpret how the programs work for fine-tuning and verification.”

items.title: AI² Robotics Joins Indonesia’s National Strategic Industries | Gasgoo
items.summary:
Underpinning this deployment is AI² Robotics's integrated "Model × Hardware × Scenario" capability. The approach centers on a brain-like embodied large model as the intelligence core, mass-producible and stable robotic bodies as the vehicle, and real-world productivity scenarios as the driving force. [...] Gasgoo Munich-On November 9, AI² Robotics announced it has signed a memorandum of understanding with the Danantara Development Management Fund (DDMF), the investment arm of Indonesia's state-backed wealth fund Danantara Indonesia. The partnership will focus on pilot applications, industrial collaboration, and local deployment of general-purpose intelligent robots and embodied AI technology across the archipelago. [...] The agreement was signed during the inaugural Danantara Technology Innovation Investment Forum (DTIIF 2026) in Jakarta, with Zhang Peng, AI² Robotics's co-founder, signing on behalf of the company.

Image Credit: AI² Robotics

Operating independently under the president's office, Danantara Indonesia holds substantial influence. AI² Robotics is now the first—and currently the only—robotics company to join DDMF's embodied AI cooperation roster.

items.title: Geek+ Unveils 24/7 Warehouse Autonomy Plan to Advance Self-Optimizing, Around-the-Clock Operation | Morningstar
items.summary: Geek+ offers a comprehensive portfolio of end-to-end warehouse robotics solutions, spanning tote-, pallet- and shelf-based workflows and applications such as material transport, storage, retrieval and order picking. Its AMR systems support high-throughput execution of structured tasks, while embodied AI is being developed to extend automation into more variable handling activities and exception recovery. Together, these capabilities form an important foundation for continuous autonomous [...] Physical AI is extending robotics beyond highly structured material-handling tasks into more complex manipulation and exception handling. Meanwhile, advances in AI are bringing greater intelligence to robot fleet coordination, warehouse workflows and day-to-day operations. Together, these developments are laying the groundwork for a new operating model: autonomous warehousing. [...] "Over the past 11 years, Geek+ has demonstrated that warehouse robotics can deliver value at scale in real operations around the world," said Yong Zheng, Founder and CEO of Geek+. "Our next goal is to enable the warehouse as a whole to operate more autonomously and continuously improve. By advancing embodied AI and warehouse-wide intelligence-and building on our global deployment capabilities-we aim to make autonomous warehouses a practical foundation for the next generation of logistics."

items.title: Weekend hack: HackerTube. I was annoyed with YouTube's recommendations so I had Claude filter down 43M comments over 20
items.summary:
Weekend hack: HackerTube. I was annoyed with YouTube's recommendations so I had Claude filter down 43M comments over 20 years of HN to 6,454 videos that keep being recommended. *Significantly* better viewing experience, ~2 hours with Opus 5.5:
https://t.co/JIhXN7OSh1

- Excellent recs without any logins (state is kept in local browser session)
- Thumbnail is a representative frame from middle of the video instead of the super duper A/B test hyper-optimized user uploads
- Underlying data from the comment analysis as one zip file, point your Claude at it and ask for your own version
- HackerTube Longs ✊

A bit more on the process:
I use Claude Code (desktop app for Mac), Opus 5.5 on Medium effort as my default. I only talk to Claude and have it do everything, the only "manual work" I helped with in tandem was in the browser (reminiscent of MenuGen): 1) I had to create some kind of API key from Google Cloud UI to query YouTube for video metadata, 2) I booted up a VPS box for serving and 3) I bought the domain name. Once the box was up I gave Claude the IP and told it update, secure, harden, deploy and optimize the code, and it did the whole thing.

Many awesome projects that would have normally taken weeks/months even can now be few-shotted for breakfast. What else are we not thinking of.

items.summary:
六个国家政府和十家 AI 公司昨天签了一份 AI 安全宣言，叫 Paris Call。签字的国家是巴林、加拿大、芬兰、法国、挪威和荷兰，公司一边有 Anthropic、微软、OpenAI、Mistral、Hugging Face 这些名字。宣言定了三件事：大家用同一套标准测评前沿模型，测评结果按统一格式公开；出事要担责，独立第三方来评估；公司要给模型装上能随时叫停的保险丝，训练中和内部使用时都能关停。宣言还留了口子，欢迎更多国家和公司加入。美国和英国这次没在签字名单里。
